claim: A shimmering volumetric column of rising heat-haze and embers glows faintly over an unseen ember bed, the air distorting and wobbling upward through depth.

q1_defects.answer: Yes, multiple defects. The 'volume' reads as a flat blocky stack of shelves, not a soft volumetric column — coarse rectangular banding/quilting is visible across the whole body. The haze also carries an unwanted green/olive cast rather than a warm glow. Compared to the soft organic edges of the ground-truth fire-flame, this looks like a low-res tiled texture.
evidence: metrics: idle bandingScore=0.251 and play-3 bandingScore=0.256 (>0.25 = visible shelf banding)
metrics: play-2 effHue=58 (yellow-green/olive) with green channel ~equal to red (effRGB 106.9,105.2,57.7)

q2_reads_as.answer: No — it does not read as rising heat-haze/embers. The body is a static olive/yellow-green blocky haze, not a glowing warm column. Against the fire-flame ground truth (a clean warm orange-to-white glow), the heat-column's dominant hue sits at ~57-58 degrees (yellow-green/olive), well outside fire's warm band (~10-45), and the green channel nearly equals red. It looks like a murky green-yellow cloud, not heat.
evidence: metrics: play-2 effHue=58 effSat=0.46 warmFrac=0.23 (vs fire band 10-45 deg high-sat)
metrics: play-1 effRGB=[109.5,106.5,58.1] (red~=green -> olive, not orange)

q3_discoverable.answer: No. The two controls a user would reach for to drive the claimed effect — 'rise' and 'wobble' — are dead. Sweeping either from low to high produces no visible change, so a first-time user dragging the labeled 'Rise' slider sees nothing happen and would conclude the tile is broken. Only the unlabeled-by-claim 'intensity' control actually does anything.
evidence: metrics: control wobble low/mid/high effRGB all identical [108.4,106.4,58.1]

q4_responsive.answer: Janky/near-dead. Across play frames the motion is minimal (frameDeltaMag ~2.8-5.6) and the frames look essentially the same olive haze, so there is no convincing sense of upward rising heat. Two of three labeled controls register no change at all, which a user reads as unresponsive.
evidence: metrics: play-1 frameDeltaMag=2.79, play-2 frameDeltaMag=2.82 (very low motion)
metrics: controls rise.changed=false and wobble.changed=false (2 of 3 controls dead)

q5_net.answer: A user would be ANNOYED: it is a static murky green-yellow blocky cloud, nothing like rising heat or embers, and dragging the Rise and Wobble sliders does nothing.

mustFix.issue: Does not read as rising heat-haze/embers — static olive/green-yellow blocky haze, dominant hue outside fire's warm band.
mustFix.evidence: heat-column/before/play-2.png : metrics play-2 effHue=58 (olive), effSat=0.46, warmFrac=0.23; green channel ~= red (effRGB 106.9,105.2,57.7)

mustFix.issue: 'Rise' control is dead — sweeping low to high produces no visible change.
mustFix.evidence: heat-column/before/control-rise-high.png vs control-rise-low.png : metrics controls rise.changed=false

mustFix.issue: 'Wobble' control is dead — low/mid/high frames are pixel-identical.
mustFix.evidence: heat-column/before/control-wobble-high.png : metrics controls wobble.changed=false, effRGB identical across sweep [108.4,106.4,58.1]

mustFix.issue: Coarse rectangular shelf banding — the 'volume' is a flat blocky tiled stack, not a soft volumetric column.

flags.note: The 'intensity' control does work and at high values pushes toward a warmer orange (effHue 42, warmFrac 0.82) — the warm look is achievable, so the olive default is a fixable choice rather than a hard limitation.
flags.evidence: metrics: control intensity high effHue=42 warmFrac=0.82; control-intensity-high.png
